title: Closed base restriction of a vanishing topos
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]), let $f:X\to S$ be of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $k:T\hookrightarrow S$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $X_T=X\times_ST$ and $f_T:X_T\to T$. Form $E_T=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ using [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. The canonical morphism $E_T\to V_f$ identifies $E_T$ with the inverse image under the second projection $p_2:V_f\to S_{\mathrm{Et}}$ of the closed subtopos $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$. The morphism $V_{f_T}\to E_T$ induced by $X_T\to X$ and $k$ is an equivalence. Here $V_f,V_{f_T}$ are as in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. Its inverse-image equivalence identifies finite-stratification constructibility on $E_T$ with that on $V_{f_T}$, both for sheaves of finite sets and for sheaves of modules over a finite commutative constant ring $\Lambda$: on $E_T$ this means finite constructible locally closed partitions of $X$ and $T$ on whose oriented products the sheaf is locally constant with finite values, as in [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf] with sets in place of modules when appropriate. Inverse image to $E_T$ preserves these constructible sheaves. The same assertions apply after replacing $X$ by any closed subscheme $Z\hookrightarrow X$, with $Z_T=Z\times_ST$.

source.place: Author draft, Lemma 8.3.1, printed p. 18, specialized to the integral morphism T closed in S, together with the rectangular restrictions in Section 8.1 and the proof of Lemma 8.3.3, printed pp. 17–19. The equivalence is the closed-immersion case of 8.3.1, not an ordinary Cartesian product of topoi.
